scenario_description:
Objective: Keep Thursday’s textile memory evening from moving a family rebozo into an unreviewed recorded story.
Emerging Need: A general story-booth notice becomes relevant only after Celia’s rebozo plan and Maren’s paid attendance are definite, then a roster proof assigns the item to audio capture.
Decision Context: Observable records establish the outing, item, order, correction address, and export cutoff; the stored caption/review note supplies the boundary between a printed label and recorded oral history.
Consequence: Timely correction can prevent an avoidable family-narrative risk while preserving attendance, and printed cards do not prevent a later opt-out before recording. The final event records an actual unreviewed first take; stopping further takes or requesting deletion remains useful.

parameter.subject: Object Memory Night: story booth preview

parameter.subject: OMN-2234 first audio take logged
parameter.body: At 18:30 the volunteer used the exported Celia Ortiz/rebozo card and recorded a first 90-second family-object story with Celia. No fresh owner review was logged before this take. The recording is held in the booth system and has not been publicly released; staff can still stop further recording and consider deletion requests.
